original_question: Which subtype of hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type I (HSAN I) is caused by a gene with a conserved globular G domain?
key_entities: hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type I

final_qi.question: Which subtype of hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type I (HSAN I) is caused by a gene with a conserved globular G domain?
final_qi.long_answer: Subtype HSAN 1B is caused by dominant mutations in the RAB7A gene. RAB7A encodes a small Ras-related GTP-binding protein whose structure is dominated by the conserved globular “G” domain characteristic of all Rab/Ras GTPases. Thus, the HSAN 1B subtype is the one linked to a gene possessing a conserved globular G domain.

final_answer.long_answer: Subtype HSAN ID is produced by pathogenic variants in the ATL3 gene. ATL3 encodes atlastin-3, a dynamin-related GTPase whose N-terminus contains a highly conserved globular “G” domain that binds and hydrolyses GTP. Mutations in this conserved G domain disrupt atlastin-3 function, leading to hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type I, subtype D (HSAN ID).
